definition: In statistical classification, Bayes error rate is the lowest possible error rate for any classifier of a random outcome (into, for example, one of two categories) and is analogous to the irreducible error.
details: A number of approaches to the estimation of the Bayes error rate exist. One method seeks to obtain analytical bounds which are inherently dependent on distribution parameters, and hence difficult to estimate. Another approach focuses on class densities, while yet another method combines and compares various classifiers. The Bayes error rate finds important use in the study of patterns and machine learning techniques.

explainer.lead: Bayes error rate is the smallest classification error that even the best possible classifier must accept for a given random outcome. It marks the irreducible part of the problem, giving researchers a reference point when studying patterns and machine learning methods.

tiers.eli5: Imagine guessing whether it will rain after looking at all the clues available. Even a perfect guesser can sometimes be wrong because the same clues can lead to different weather. The Bayes error rate is the smallest number of mistakes any guesser could possibly make on average.
tiers.practitioner: It serves as a theoretical error floor when assessing classifiers, rather than as a score produced by training a model. Estimation approaches include analytical bounds, methods based on class densities, and methods that combine and compare classifiers. Bounds can depend on distribution parameters that are difficult to estimate, so an observed test error should not be treated as a direct measurement of this floor.
tiers.paperLevel: For features X and a categorical label Y, the Bayes classifier predicts argmax_c P(Y=c | X=x), and its error is R* = E_X[1 - max_c P(Y=c | X=x)]. This is the minimum achievable error over classifiers using X and represents irreducible error. Estimation is difficult when analytical bounds require unknown distribution parameters or when class densities must be estimated.

explainer.example: Suppose that for a particular input, the probability of category A is 0.8 and the probability of category B is 0.2. The best prediction is A, with an unavoidable error of 0.2 for that input; averaging the corresponding minimum errors over all inputs gives the Bayes error rate.

usedIn.name: Classifier comparison studies

explainer.intuition: Some mistakes are unavoidable when the available information does not uniquely determine the outcome. Bayes error rate measures that unavoidable remainder after giving the classification task to the best possible classifier.
howItWorks: Specify the inputs, possible categories, and random outcome.
For each input, identify the category with the highest conditional probability.
The remaining probability at that input is the smallest possible error there.
Average these minimum errors across inputs to obtain the Bayes error rate.
explainer.whyItMatters: It separates error that no classifier can remove from error that might be reduced through better classification methods. This makes it an important reference in pattern recognition and machine learning.
misconceptions: It is not the measured error of one trained classifier.
It need not be zero, even with an ideal classifier.
It is generally estimated rather than read directly from a test score.
